description: The three common ways to reach the Antarctic Peninsula compared: sailing from Ushuaia, flying from Punta Arenas to King George Island (fly-cruise), and the long route via the Falklands and South Georgia. Crossing time, days on the ice and trip length, each with its source.
caption: Departure ports and routes compared. Trip lengths and days on the ice are taken from one published example itinerary per route (operator sources, marked); other departures differ. Distances are great-circle figures we calculated, not sailed or flown routes.
legend: Operator figures come from a single company's published itinerary and are an example, not an average. Southbound does not rank or recommend these operators by citing them.

crossing.text: By ship across the Drake Passage, out and back.

distance.text: About 1,008 km (544 nautical miles) to Deception Island, South Shetlands, in a straight line.

time.text: About two days each way at sea (example itinerary).

ice.text: 5 days (days 4–8 of 11) in the South Shetlands and on the Peninsula (example itinerary).

weather.text: Open-ocean crossing in the belt of strong westerly winds.

note.text: Most Antarctic voyages run on the Peninsula and depart from Ushuaia or, to a lesser extent, other ports.

routes.name: Punta Arenas: fly-cruise via King George Island

crossing.text: By air from Punta Arenas to the Teniente R. Marsh airstrip on King George Island, both ways; the ship is boarded there.

distance.text: About 1,225 km (661 nautical miles) Punta Arenas to the Marsh airstrip, in a straight line.

time.text: About 2 hours (operator charter) to about 2.5 hours (DAP King Air), weather permitting.

ice.text: Days 2–7 of 8, with four full cruising days (days 3–6) (example itinerary).

length.text: 8 days / 7 nights (example itinerary); shorter and longer versions are sold.

weather.text: Flights and activities depend on weather and flight restrictions; delays are possible.

note.text: IAATO recorded 170 southbound flights into the Marsh airstrip supporting 126 air-cruise voyages in 2025-26.

routes.name: Ushuaia: Falklands, South Georgia and Antarctica

crossing.text: By ship: Ushuaia to the Falklands, on to South Georgia, then south, returning across the Drake Passage.

distance.text: About 1,452 km (784 nautical miles) Stanley to Grytviken, in a straight line. South Georgia is about 800 miles south-east of the Falklands.

time.text: Two sea days Stanley to South Georgia; two sea days back to Ushuaia at the end (example itinerary).

ice.text: South Georgia days 7–10, South Orkneys day 12, Weddell Sea and Antarctic waters days 15–16, of 19, depending on ice (example itinerary).

weather.text: Long open-ocean sections; South Georgia landings need a GSGSSI entry permit, usually arranged by the operator.

note.text: St Andrews Bay holds South Georgia's largest king penguin colony.

notes.heading: Ross Sea voyages
notes.html: The Ross Sea, on the other side of the continent, is reached from New Zealand or Australia rather than South America. One published example is a 28-day voyage from Bluff, New Zealand. The Ross Sea region Marine Protected Area, covering 1.55 million km², was established on 1 December 2017. See the regions guide.

notes.heading: How distances were calculated
notes.html: Great-circle (shortest straight-line) distance between the two points, using the haversine formula with an Earth radius of 6,371 km. Ships and aircraft do not fly or sail these exact lines.
